siblings.title: Is Redux still the right answer for a new React 19 app in 2026?
siblings.summary: Redux is healthy but no longer the default: for a greenfield React 19 SPA talking to a REST API, TanStack Query plus a small Zustand store wins.

siblings.title: Server-state layer for a React 19 + Vite SPA on a .NET API: TanStack Query wins
siblings.summary: TanStack Query is the correct server-state layer for itenium-ui; Register.defaultError makes RFC 9457 ProblemDetails a first-class typed error.

siblings.title: Generating the itenium-ui API client from Forge's OpenAPI document
siblings.summary: Orval emits TanStack Query hooks, query keys, MSW mocks and Zod schemas from one config.

siblings.title: The router is a state manager: TanStack Router for itenium-ui
siblings.summary: TanStack Router makes filters/sort/pagination typed URL state instead of Redux slices.

siblings.title: Auth & session state for a React 19 SPA on Forge: kill the localStorage plan
siblings.summary: Use react-oidc-context with an in-memory access token and put roles behind a /me query.

sources.title: TanStack Query — Does this replace client state?
sources.claim: Once async code moves to TanStack Query, the remaining truly-global client state is usually tiny — typically just themeMode and sidebarStatus.

sources.title: State of React 2025 — State management
sources.claim: Zustand is gaining fast and leads on satisfaction; many respondents use no state library at all.

sources.title: React state management in 2026 (bundle sizes & downloads)
sources.claim: 2026 gzip sizes: Zustand 1.2 KB, Valtio 3.2 KB, Jotai 3.5 KB, RTK 12 KB; Zustand 22.6M weekly downloads vs RTK 11.4M, Jotai 2.9M, Valtio 1.2M; Recoil archived by Meta in early 2025.

sources.claim: React 19 ships useActionState, useOptimistic and useFormStatus, absorbing pending/error/optimistic state for form-shaped mutations.

sources.title: Zustand — Comparison
sources.claim: Zustand is a single immutable store with no context provider required; render optimization is manual via selectors.

sources.title: Jotai — Comparison
sources.claim: Jotai is bottom-up atomic composition; context-first, module-second, whereas Zustand is module-first.

sources.title: Zustand — Testing guide
sources.claim: Zustand's official Jest recipe uses a __mocks__/zustand.ts that collects reset functions and resets every store in afterEach; stores can be driven directly.

sources.title: Jotai — Testing guide
sources.claim: Testing Jotai atoms in isolation means creating a store with createStore() and reading atoms via store.get / store.set.

sources.title: Zustand — persist middleware
sources.claim: persist supports localStorage, partialize, versioning/migrate, merge and skipHydration.

sources.title: Zustand — Migrating to v5
sources.claim: v5 uses useSyncExternalStore semantics: a selector returning a fresh object reference triggers an infinite render loop unless wrapped in useShallow.

sources.title: zustand discussion #2790 — Infinite loop error with V5
sources.claim: Community reports of 'Maximum update depth exceeded' after the v5 upgrade caused by object-returning selectors.

sources.title: Nx — Enforce module boundaries
sources.claim: Nx enforces architecture via project tags plus the @nx/enforce-module-boundaries ESLint rule with depConstraints.

sources.title: Nx module boundaries in practice
sources.claim: The Nx boundary rule works at project level only, not folder level.

sources.title: React — useSyncExternalStore
sources.claim: useSyncExternalStore is React's official primitive for subscribing to an external store.

sources.title: Jotai — Using store outside React
sources.claim: Jotai's createStore gives a store usable outside React, enabling non-component tests.

sources.title: Stately — @xstate/store
sources.claim: @xstate/store is a small event-based store, framework-agnostic, comparable to Zustand/Redux.

sources.title: How Valtio proxy state works (React part)

sources.title: Jotai — Provider
sources.claim: Jotai works provider-less by default but a Provider is needed for per-subtree/per-test store isolation.
